clips.send: Someone just got a normal cholesterol test sends this to a parent who assumes that means their heart is fine - a little anxiety that the real test was never ordered.
clips.caption:
Kevin Trudeau called a top Harvard-trained cardiologist and asked for a CAT scan with contrast, an ultrasound on his heart, and a full-body vascular test. No symptoms, just wanting to actually look.

The doctor's answer: insurance won't cover that without symptoms. Instead, he ran a cholesterol number - 225 - and wanted to prescribe a statin to bring it to 220.

Kevin Trudeau's question: does a cholesterol number tell you if you actually have a blockage? The doctor admitted it doesn't, and admitted those deeper tests only happen after someone already has chest pains or numbness.

Has your doctor ever ordered anything beyond a cholesterol number?
